title: Supervised Classification Algorithm Selection
description: Decision framework for selecting optimal tabular classification algorithms based on dataset size, linearity, and explainability.
conditions: Supervised classification task with binary or multiclass categorical targets
Requirement to balance predictive accuracy with model interpretability
recommended_methods: Logistic Regression with L2 (Ridge) regularization as the transparent baseline
Gradient Boosted Trees (LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost) for state-of-the-art tabular accuracy
Random Forest for robust non-linear modeling with minimal hyperparameter tuning
selection_rules: If strict legal or clinical explainability is mandated, choose Logistic Regression with weight inspection
If maximizing ROC-AUC or Log-Loss on complex tabular data, choose LightGBM or XGBoost
If dataset has high percentage of categorical features with high cardinality, choose CatBoost
limitations: Gradient boosting models are susceptible to overfitting on small noisy datasets (N < 500)
Logistic regression fails to capture complex feature interactions without manual polynomial engineering
